title: feat(wire): request the Ra 0.35 work quality for one 20 mm punch
body:
Stacked on #2978. Review the [quality changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/124be7caf9a9b37f79f34bf30394a7db6e765f89...17cb6f617460627b543f160f0e06821a752bac27).

Process change: yes

## What changed

This PR is ported onto the zero-step setup of #2984. The job names the requested work quality. It arms no technology. The operator assigns TECCUT on the control after the review, as for every other job.

- The new Wire Contour condition `AGIE_BERCO_RA035` requests quality `CCB035`: Ra 0.35, Te 1.50 and Tkm 1.00 µm, with the speed option set and the other two options disabled: `JE_CreateQuality(je_piece,"CCB035","0.35,1.50,1.00,T,F,F",je_q1)`. With the speed option, the control preselects the Ra 0.35 technology `estbca25nsn060b035020` (TECCUT header `TYPE:VS`). The job still arms no technology. The condition `AGIE_QN2` requests `CCB030`, as before.
- `camcraft_post::agie_setup::Quality` (`Ccb030`, `Ccb035`) is on the private `Piece`. The piece creates one quality object with that name. `PunchSetup20::encode_quality` is the only way to request `CCB035`. `encode`, `encode_die`, `PunchGroup20` and `CutoffSetup20` keep `CCB030`.
- `CCB035_OFFSETS_UM` has one row: 20 mm, five passes, 234, 189, 154, 139 and 129 µm (main cut and four trims). `Quality::offsets_um` returns all passes, and `Quality::rough_um` gives the main cut. The contour checks (clearance, miter and entry) use the main-cut offset of the selected quality: 234 µm for `CCB035`. The 0.4 mm stock margin does not change (0.234 + 0.125 rounds up to 0.4). `CCB030` keeps its 4-pass table and its bytes.
- The operator review of `CCB035` names the technology `estbca25nsn060b035020`, the header `TYPE:VS`, 5 passes and the five offsets. It tells the operator to stop if one of them is different. The user guide says the same. It names the technology, not a TECCUT number: the first TECCUT column is a match distance, not a row id.
- `camcraft_post::agie::export_punch_with_review` takes the quality. With `Ccb030` it is `export_with_review`.
- The app refuses `AGIE_BERCO_RA035` for a punch group and for a DXF circle or racetrack. The post refuses other stock thicknesses, a die opening and an open cutoff. No directory is written.
- The old script writer (`jescript.rs`) is gone on the frame. The old `AgieQuality` type is replaced by `Quality`.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2966-agie-fine-quality.md`. User guide: "Request Ra 0.35 µm for one 20 mm punch".

## Value sources

- Ra 0.35, Te 1.50 and Tkm 1.00: the Fine+ values of the MIT Agie Processor quality presets, as in the original PR.
- The speed flag and the offsets 234, 189, 154, 139 and 129 µm at 20 mm: the control measurement of 25 Nov (`Camcraft-notes/agie-imports-20261125/FINE20-0289/summary.txt`) and the control check of this head (below). The user decided the change.
- The quality name `CCB035` follows `CCB030` (#2984: a generic name can bind other resident data).

## Readings on the emulated Classic Cut 2S: the speed flag (folder 25 Nov)

Job `FINE20` from `examples/agie/fine-punch.camscript` on this head. These are the golden files. The SBL is byte-identical to the probe SBL of the 25 Nov measurement. Evidence: the maintainer's notes folder `agie-imports-20261125/FINE20-new/` (screenshots, J00, summary). Throwaway clone of `practice-color-ready`; the base image SHA-256 did not change.

- The ISO and the SBL arrived on the control byte for byte.
- After import: `CUT1 - CCB035[0]`. FORMALCHECK gave one error, `Technologie : te definiëren`.
- Work Details: quality `CCB035`, Ra 0.35 µm, Tkm 1.0 µm, Te 1.5 µm, "Snelheid" (speed) on, "Hoge kwaliteit" off.
- TECCUT header: `M:x123 Mat:Fe Maf:BC TYPE:VS Dia:0.25 H:20 Ra:0.35 Tkm:1.0 Te:1.5`. The control preselected technology `estbca25nsn060b035020` (type S, 5 passes; shown with Dis 0199).
- After Assign, with no manual row choice: `CCB035[5]`, T100 on each pass, offsets 234 (main), 189, 154, 139 and 129 µm.
- FORMALCHECK: `Controleresultaat: geen fouten`. With warnings on: `Uitgekozen opties : 131584` and `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren` only.
- GRAFICHECK (J00, 9602 bytes): 5 passes in the main loop and 5 in the 1.000 mm separation. The face offsets are X ±20.234, ±20.189, ±20.154, ±20.139 and ±20.129, equal to the table. The J00 is byte-identical to the J00 of the 25 Nov probe.

## Earlier readings without the speed flag (2026-11-24, superseded)

Job `FINE20` from `examples/agie/fine-punch.camscript`. These are the golden files.

- The ISO and the SBL arrived on the control byte for byte.
- After import: `CUT1 - CCB035[0]`. FORMALCHECK gave one error, `Technologie : te definiëren`.
- Work Details: quality `CCB035`, Ra 0.35 µm, Tkm 1.0 µm, Te 1.5 µm. The two visible options were off.
- TECCUT header: `M:x123 Mat:Fe Maf:BC TYPE:V Dia:0.25 H:20 Ra:0.35 Tkm:1.0 Te:1.5`.
- The control preselected row 0204: 4 passes, technology `estbca25nnn060b030020`. This is the Ra 0.30 technology that `CCB030` also preselects. The table also has row 0289, `estbca25nsn060b035020`: type S, 5 passes, Ra 0.35. The control did not preselect it. It was not assigned, and its offsets are not measured.
- After the assignment of row 0204: `CCB035[4]`, T100 on each pass, offsets 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm.
- FORMALCHECK: `geen fouten`. With warnings on: `Uitgekozen opties : 131072` and `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren` only.
- GRAFICHECK: the trace is the same as the trace of the 15 mm `CCB030` punch, except Z. The separation is 1.000 mm.

Result of that run: without the speed flag, the control preselected the Ra 0.30 technology. The speed flag above corrects this. No physical cut was made, so the surface Ra is not measured.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` lib, `agie::quality_tests`:
  - `ccb035_changes_only_the_quality_line_of_a_20_mm_punch`
  - `ccb030_through_the_quality_export_keeps_every_byte`
  - `ccb035_refuses_other_heights_sides_and_separations_without_files`
  - `the_setup_encoder_holds_ccb035_to_20_mm`
- `camcraft-post` lib, `agie::quality_tests::ccb035_has_five_measured_passes_and_keeps_the_0_4_mm_margin` (new: the 5-entry table, the main-cut offset and the 0.4 mm margin).
- `camcraft-app` test `agie_native`, module `quality` (moved from the binary `agie_quality`):
  - `the_saved_condition_selects_the_exact_requested_quality` (save, load, FINE20 golden)
  - `ra035_refuses_unmeasured_heights_without_a_directory` (15, 40 and 80 mm)
  - `ra035_refuses_a_group_an_arc_punch_a_die_and_a_cutoff` (each example posts with `AGIE_QN2`, and is refused with `AGIE_BERCO_RA035`)
- The goldens that main already has (CCSEP20, DIE20 and the inspection goldens) do not change. Other goldens are listed in "Goldens moved". Existing tests pass unchanged.

## Gate (head `688f776e0`)

The head merges `origin/main` at `aedd9750c` (through the #2978 head), which has the fix of #3774.

- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: batch fallback (geometry is in the stack diff). 1201 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (42.1 min). `agie_native` (28 tests), `agie_safe_setup`, `script_agie_native`, `example_catalog*` and the `post`, `app` and `ui` lib tests passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main`: clean.
- No heavy lane ran (this PR is not `P1`).

## Not exercised

- A physical cut. The surface Ra is not measured.
- Other heights, a die, an open cutoff, a group and a DXF arc punch with `CCB035`. They are refused.

Changelog: The native wire EDM job can request work quality CCB035 (Ra 0.35 µm, speed option) for one closed polygon punch on 20 mm steel with Berco Cut 0.25 mm wire. The control then preselects the 5-pass Ra 0.35 technology. The job arms no technology.

## UI screenshots

This PR contains the two open-cutoff controls of #2972 on the Wire Contour Passes tab. One pair of images covers all five PRs of the stack. The reviewer rendered the images with the crate's egui_kittest harness.

Before (main):

![Before: Wire Contour Passes tab on main](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr-2972/wire-open-cutoff-before.png?raw=true)

After (with the two cutoff controls):

![After: Wire Contour Passes tab with the two cutoff controls](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr-2972/wire-open-cutoff-after.png?raw=true)

## Goldens moved

The golden files below are additions relative to main. This PR changes no golden file that main already has. The goldens CCSEP20 and DIE20 of main do not change.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/CIRCLE20.ISO` (A): pins the ISO of a placed circle DXF job. Added by #2978 of the stack.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/FINE20.ISO` (A): pins the ISO of the FINE20 job with quality CCB035. Added by #2979 of the stack.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/FINE20.SBL` (A): pins the SBL of the FINE20 job with quality CCB035. Added by #2979 of the stack. Its quality line requests `0.35,1.50,1.00,T,F,F` (the speed flag). It differs from the renamed `CCSEP20.SBL` in that one line only.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/FINE20.SBR` (A): pins the SBR of the FINE20 job with quality CCB035. Added by #2979 of the stack.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/RACE20.ISO` (A): pins the ISO of a placed racetrack DXF job. Added by #2978 of the stack.
- `crates/post/tests/golden/agie-setup/LOWER20.SBL` (A): pins the open-cutoff (zero-step, one cut) setup SBL. Added by #2972 of the stack.
- `crates/post/tests/golden/agie-setup/PAIR20.SBL` (A): pins the SBL of a group of two punches on one plate. Added by #2974 of the stack.
- `crates/post/tests/golden/agie-setup/PAIR20.SBR` (A): pins the SBR of a group of two punches on one plate. Added by #2974 of the stack.

## Test layout

This PR adds no new top-level test binary. The new tests of the stack are modules of existing suites. The test count did not change.

- `crates/app/tests/agie_quality.rs` moved to `crates/app/tests/agie_native/quality.rs`: module `quality` of `agie_native`, 3 tests. The suite now has 28 tests (25 + 3). The `agie_native` Gate map covers `app::posting::agie`.
- `crates/post/tests/agie_cutoff_setup.rs` (from #2972) and `crates/post/tests/agie_group_setup.rs` (from #2974) are the modules `cutoff` and `group` of `agie_safe_setup` (16 tests).
- The tests are unchanged except for the golden and example paths, and the one expected quality line of the FINE20 check (the speed flag).
